messages:
alexa: Quick follow-up on continuous batching scheduler tradeoffs — we need alignment on routing/queue interfaces for sustained payloads. I'm worried current enqueue contract leaks too little info for good packing, but exposing too much invites client gaming.

matt: Can you lay out the concrete options you see?

alexa: Short version: two orthogonal axes. 1) routing surface: lane-based (dedicated lanes per tenant/priority) vs shared-queue with dynamic shaping. 2) caller surface: opaque enqueue (server estimates) vs explicit shape+deadline hints. Tradeoffs: isolation and predictable SLOs vs utilization. Also: preemption semantics + KV-cache handoff.

ranjit: We ran a prototype with optional shape hints. For long sequences it shaved ~7-12% per-token latency (better packing). But that prototype starved small, low-latency requests unless we enforced strict headroom for the small-lane.

lucy: Exposing shape_hint to external clients seems risky — customers will try to optimize requests and that undermines fairness. I prefer server-side estimation with a telemetry trust score used to weigh client hints.

matt: Hybrid sounds promising. Proposal: accept optional shape_hint but mark it "advisory". Admission API returns an estimate and a ticket. If telemetry shows mismatch > threshold, demote the hint and emit an alert.

alexa: Implementation sketch for API (pseudo):
```
Enqueue(req_id, size_bytes, deadline_ms, shape_hint=null, priority="normal")
-> { status: "OK", ticket_id: "t-123", estimated_wait_ms: 12 }
```
Key behavior: shape_hint used only if server confidence >= 0.8, otherwise server-estimate overrides.

sam: On preemption/eviction we need to pin KV-cache for in-flight sequences. Otherwise preempt -> evict -> regenerate causes huge CPU spike. Suggested: eviction signal includes preemptible flag + checkpoint callback that runtime can use to persist KV slices for quick reload.

alexa: Proposed eviction handshake: 1) scheduler sends preempt-intent for ticket_id with grace_ms; 2) runtime tries checkpoint KV; 3) if checkpoint acked within grace, scheduler requeues with preserved KV handle; else force-evict. This is soft-preempt semantics.

ranjit: Metrics we should emit: queue_length_by_lane, avg_wait_ms_p50/p99, preemption_count_by_tenant, kv_miss_rate_after_preempt, shape_hint_discrepancy_rate. Also tag by model_variant and route.

lucy: Operational note: expose per-route SLA dashboard and automated fallback maps (route X -> fallback model Y when expected latency > threshold). That mapping should be part of rollout config.

matt: Question about backpressure: token-bucket at enqueue layer vs early-reject on admission? For tight SLOs we should early-reject noisy tenants instead of letting them pile up and cause long tails. Early-reject also avoids wasting KV checkpoint effort.

alexa: I agree — early-reject policy + limited queue reservation for small-latency requests. Reserve slots by token size buckets. Policy: if enqueue rejected, return retry-after + reason code.

ci-bot: build: scheduler-protos v2 passed unit + integration tests :white_check_mark:

alexa: Next actions/checklist:
- interface sketch + proto PR (matt)
- simulation runs: hybrid routing (ranjit)
- telemetry and dashboard proto (lucy)
- kv-checkpoint handshake impl notes (sam)
- update RFC with decisions and tradeoffs (alexa)

matt: I'll own the proto sketch, will post WIP by EOD tomorrow.

ranjit: I'll spin up sim with mixed short+long workloads and the advisory-shape path.

lucy: I'll draft dashboard panels and alert rules for shape_discrepancy and preemptions.

sam: I'll draft the checkpoint handshake sequence diagram and add failure modes.

alexa: Cool. If no objections, I'll fold this into the RFC follow-up doc. :thumbsup:

matt: +1

ranjit: +1

lucy: +1

alexa: tagging followups: @matt @ranjit @lucy @sam — thanks.
